title: STRANGE MINUTE #14 · WHAT IF

lines.text: What if you spent just one day on Mercury?
A probe just got there, after an eight-year trip.
First problem: one day there lasts 176 Earth days.
lines.say: First problem: one day there lasts a hundred seventy-six Earth days.

lines.text: Its whole year is only 88 days.
lines.say: Its whole year is only eighty-eight days.

lines.text: So from sunrise to sunset, a full year goes by.
The Sun looks almost three times bigger.
At noon, the ground hits 800 degrees Fahrenheit.
lines.say: At noon, the ground hits eight hundred degrees Fahrenheit.

lines.text: That's hot enough to melt lead.
At night it drops to minus 290. No air holds the heat.
lines.say: At night it drops to minus two hundred ninety. No air holds the heat.

lines.text: In some spots, the Sun rises, dips back, then rises again.
And yet, deep in its polar craters, there's ice.
So, would you rather take Mercury's day, or its night?
